page: Amazon Web Services r7g.large is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by custom AWS Graviton processors. Built on the 64-bit ARM64 architecture with Neoverse-V1 cores, this instance features 2 dedicated physical cores and 2 vCPUs running at 2.6 GHz. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates moderate single-core performance alongside lower multi-core efficiency. The stress-ng single-core CPU test scores 1532.49, which sits in the average range, while the multi-core score drops to 3040.96. Large-block read memory bandwidth reaches 53.89 GB/sec, though write bandwidth is lower at 20.68 GB/sec. The instance demonstrates weaker performance in multi-threaded decompression, database operations, and LLM inference, with Redis SET operations executing at 3.35 million operations per second.

The r7g.large does not include local NVMe storage, relying entirely on network-attached storage options. Network connectivity is limited to a baseline bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Given the high memory allocation relative to the limited compute resources, this instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require intensive parallel processing. It is best suited for caching layers, lightweight database operations, and memory-intensive general-purpose applications.
description: Amazon Web Services r7g.large is an ARM64 memory-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton Neoverse-V1 processors. Operating on the Nitro hypervisor, it features 2 dedicated physical cores (2 vCPUs) running at 2.6 GHz and 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a high 8.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance lacks local storage and features a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps. Performance benchmarks show average single-core CPU capabilities and memory read bandwidth, but weaker multi-core scaling and memory write speeds. The processor includes a 32 MB L3 cache and supports AES cryptography, but lacks AVX and AMX extensions. The r7g.large is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-heavy workloads with low parallel processing demands, making it suitable for caching layers, small database instances, and memory-bound application servers.
